title: Batcher slot freeze: runaway sleeping slots and guardrail playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: During a capacity surge on 2026-02-09 we observed a new failure mode where batcher slots entered a 'sleeping' state and did not wake for extended periods, causing batch formation stalls and 99th percentile latency spikes for small, latency-sensitive requests. This ticket tracks the investigation, short-term mitigations, and long-term guardrails to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-02-09 02:41 UTC - On-call alerted: increased 95/99 latency in hosted-west region for text-generation route.
2026-02-09 02:48 UTC - Initial mitigation: scaled dedicated pool up 2x to reduce queueing; latency improved but tail spikes persisted.
2026-02-09 03:15 UTC - Engineering collected heap profiles and batcher debug traces; observed large numbers of slots in 'sleeping' state with no heartbeat.
2026-02-10 09:00 UTC - Root-cause hypothesis formed: a backpressure change in upstream prioritization combined with timer drift caused slot sleepers to miss wakeup window.
2026-02-11 14:30 UTC - Deployed emergency hotfix: added watchdog that probes sleeping slots every 50 ms; immediate reduction in tail latency.
2026-02-17 12:00 UTC - Ongoing: implementing invariant checks and controlled rollout of permanent fixes.
impact_summary: ~7% of requests for the affected route saw 99th percentile latency increase from ~220ms to >3s during peak. Affected deployments: hosted-west and dedicated-pool-3. No data loss; customers experienced retries, increased latency, and occasional client-side timeouts. customer_impact: medium.
root_cause: Combination of factors: (1) upstream prioritizer change that concentrated microbursts into latency lanes, (2) timer wheel drift in the slot scheduler under heavy GC/CPU pauses causing slots to miss wake deadlines, (3) absence of a recovery path for slots that missed multiple heartbeats. These allowed sleeping slots to accumulate and prevented new batch formation for latency-sensitive lanes.
short_term_mitigation: Hotfix: slot-watchdog probes and force-wake for slots that miss >3 heartbeats (deployed 2026-02-11). Configured conservative backpressure throttle to smooth microbursts. Increased monitoring thresholds and alerting for sleeping-slot counts.
long_term_plan: Replace single timer wheel with per-core high-resolution timers to reduce wake drift under GC and CPU contention.
Add an explicit fairness qdisc that caps slot residency time for latency lanes so individual slots can be evicted to avoid accumulation.
Implement deterministic slot state machine tests in CI that simulate GC pauses and microbursts to catch regressions early.
Expose a Console config knob to adjust watchdog sensitivity per-customer and add RBAC for enterprise tuning.

acceptance_criteria: No occurrences of batcher.slot_sleep_count > 5 per-host under 99th-percentile load in staged runs.
System sustains target QPS with <= 2x baseline 99th latency under simulated GC pauses.
Dashboards show per-lane wake/recovery time and alerts fire for abnormal drift and are actionable.
monitoring_and_alerting: New metrics: batcher.slot_sleep_count, batcher.slot_missed_heartbeats, batcher.slot_force_wakes. Alert: slot_sleep_count > 3 for > 30s in any host -> P1. Added synthetic latency probe for small requests every 15s. Retain debug traces for 90 days for incident investigations.
postmortem_notes: Trade-offs: aggressive watchdog reduces tail latency but can increase CPU wake churn; we chose a conservative threshold and will tune based on load tests.
We debated enforcing fairness by scheduler admission vs eviction; short-term eviction chosen to reduce blast radius while designing a scheduler-level solution.
Customer comms: status page updated and targeted emails sent to the top affected customers with mitigation details and ETA for permanent fixes.
